PullRequest.Title: Add Agents Window taskbar shortcut and icons
PullRequest.Body: - Add an **Agents Window** task to the Windows taskbar jump list - Launch it through the existing `--agents` mode - Use the distro-mixed `sessions.ico` asset for the jump-list task and resulting Windows taskbar button, so Stable, Insiders, and Exploration receive matching product-quality branding - Expose each native `CodeWindow` icon path through generic opened-window metadata - Have **Switch Window** render the icon advertised by the window, preserving existing file and workspace icons when a native icon is not provided ### Screenshots ### Related issues Fixes #335321 Fixes #315734 Fixes #315935

Scenarios.Scenario: Windows startup and recent-workspace changes refresh the taskbar jump list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial refresh runs only at LifecycleMainPhase.Eventually, explicitly outside startup's primary critical path. Later refreshes follow recently-opened changes. Each refresh must finish storage lookup/JSON restoration and the existing Electron jump-list calls before that refresh completes, but application/window progress does not await event-triggered refreshes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse the recently-opened application-shared storage value
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read before the recent-workspace branch and one reread after removal handling when filtered workspaces exist; before the diff the same scenario performed up to three reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior implementation called getRecentlyOpened for the condition and again for item construction, plus the read inside removeRecentlyOpened.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks only the deferred jump-list refresh, not initial workbench readiness; event-triggered refreshes are not awaited by callers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query Windows jump-list settings through Electron app.getJumpListSettings
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per refresh and only when a non-Agent recent workspace remains after filtering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Called once whenever any recent workspace existed, including an Agent sessions workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous native work on the main process during the deferred refresh; placement and call count are unchanged or reduced when only Agent recents exist.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install the jump-list categories through Electron app.setJumpList
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly once per refresh, unchanged; payload gains one constant task item and icon path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same native call installed tasks, bounded workspace entries, and the recent category without the Agents task.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks completion of the deferred refresh but does not gate workbench startup or window interaction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most 500 retained recent workspaces are canonicalized and filtered; only jumpListSettings.minItems entries are materialized. The new filter is linear over the bounded workspace list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The initial refresh is awaited by handleWindowsJumpList; change-event refreshes remain unawaited and may overlap as before. The diff neither increases event frequency nor changes coalescing/backpressure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Application storage is awaited once for readiness; subsequent reads use the storage service value and parse the bounded recents payload. The diff reuses the first filtered result and reduces the prior worst-case getRecentlyOpened calls from three to two when recents exist. No new cache or invalidation path is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the lifecycle registration, bounded recent-history constant, storage call path, and unchanged native call sites.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Electron's exact native cost for one additional task item is platform-dependent, but it is constant-sized and does not alter refresh frequency or effective concurrency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added task is constant-size, filtering is bounded, and the refactor removes one repeated recent-history read on the nonempty path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Creating an Agents Window on Windows with a dedicated taskbar icon
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Path construction and assigning options.icon happen immediately before new electron.BrowserWindow(options), so any Electron icon file resolution/decoding is on that individual window's creation path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Electron may resolve and decode the packaged sessions.ico supplied as BrowserWindowOptions.icon
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fixed local icon per created Agents window; zero for ordinary windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No explicit sessions.ico path was supplied; Electron used the existing default window/application icon behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Potentially contributes a single small local-resource load to Agents-window construction, alongside BrowserWindow creation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixed sessions.ico resource per Agents BrowserWindow creation; normal editor windows do not execute the icon assignment.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Window construction is synchronous per CodeWindow on the Electron main process. The diff adds no loops, queues, or parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The JavaScript path/URI values are constructed once per CodeWindow. Electron or OS icon caching is not explicit in repository code, so cold decode behavior is uncertain; no application-level repeated lookup exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the option is newly supplied on the constructor path; low evidence of any material latency because the work is constant and required by the visual feature.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The read/decode may be internally cached by Electron or Windows, but even cold it is a single packaged icon and not collection- or event-scaled.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this is bounded, intentional work necessary to provide the requested native icon, with no realistic amplification mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoking Switch Window while an Agents Window is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action awaits the existing nativeHostService.getWindows IPC, constructs one pick per open window, and renders visible quick-pick rows. A sessions icon can be fetched/decoded by the renderer when its row is rendered.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch opened-window metadata from the main process
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per switch-window invocation, returning one record per open window; the payload adds one small URI only for each Agents window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request returned ids, workspace metadata, titles, filenames, and dirty state without iconPath.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing IPC must complete before the picker appears; the added constant metadata does not add another IPC or round trip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Renderer resolves the file URI used as the quick-pick row background image
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one stable sessions.ico resource per renderer cache, referenced by rendered Agents-window rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agents-window rows used computed workspace/file icon classes and did not reference sessions.ico.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Image display may complete asynchronously after row construction; no synchronous repository file read was added to BaseSwitchWindow.run.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Window enumeration remains O(number of main and auxiliary windows). The new URI is present only for Agents windows and points to one constant resource; normal windows retain existing icon-class computation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One existing getWindows request per action invocation. Quick-pick row rendering is synchronous; resource fetch/decode is browser-managed rather than a new explicit Promise fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resource URI is stable. Browser resource caching may make subsequent picker opens warm, but even without that cache each affected row references the same packaged icon. No unbounded icon-class cache entry is created because list rows set backgroundImage directly.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the IPC producer, action consumer, and quick-input renderer call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact browser image-cache and ICO decode timing is not visible here, but cardinality is bounded to a stable local asset and ordinary window rows are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: metadata growth is tiny, no extra boundary round trip is introduced, and icon loading is bounded to a stable local resource rather than scaling with arbitrary window paths.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The package task copies the newly listed icon with the other static Windows icon assets; this affects build/package generation, not editor runtime startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy resources/win32/sessions.ico into the Windows package
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional file per Windows packaging run.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The sessions icon was not included in the package resource list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds only the fixed asset copy to the existing packaging stream.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional fixed binary asset per packaged Windows build.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Uses the existing package resource stream; the diff adds no new task or subprocess.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Build-stream caching behavior is unchanged; there is no runtime cache lifecycle change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the package resource-list hunk.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Binary size is not exposed by the textual patch, but it is a single ICO alongside existing icons and there is no scaling mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the build-time and package-size cost is fixed and necessary for the added icon.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all nine changed files, including the binary asset inventory. Traced deferred jump-list updates, Agents-window construction, opened-window IPC, quick-pick rendering, and packaging. The diff adds only bounded icon work and constant metadata, while reducing repeated recent-history reads; no high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.
